Beer
BEER
proper noun
Hebrew be’ēr, “a well,” here a proper name; a station of Israel where the LORD gave them water, and a town whither Jotham fled.

Biblical Definition

Beer, simply “the well,” is the name of a station of Israel beyond Arnon, where the LORD gave His people water and they sang for joy. “And from thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the LORD spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water” (Num 21:16). Then Israel sang this song, “Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it: the princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver, with their staves” (Num 21:17-18). It is one of the few songs of the wilderness, a song over water, when the thirsting host saw the LORD bring forth a fountain in the desert. This same name Beer is borne also by a town whither Jotham, the youngest son of Gideon, fled and dwelt for fear of Abimelech his brother, after he had spoken his parable of the trees (Judg 9:21). The place, the well, is a memorial of the kindness of God to His thirsting people. He did not give them water grudgingly, but drew from them a song; and the digging of the well by the staves of the princes shows that the LORD is pleased to use the obedience of His people in bringing forth the streams of His grace. Beer witnesses that where God gathers His people and gives them water, there shall be singing.

Webster 1828 Definition

The station where the LORD gave Israel water and they sang “Spring up, O well”; also a town whither Jotham fled.

expand to see more

BEER, a proper name signifying “a well,” a station of Israel beyond Arnon.

There the LORD gave the thirsting people water, as He had promised Moses.

Israel sang over it, Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it.

The princes and nobles digged the well by the direction of the lawgiver.

A town of the same name was the refuge of Jotham from Abimelech (Judg 9:21).

Key Scripture

Num 21:16 — "And from thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the LORD spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water."

Num 21:17 — "Then Israel sang this song, Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it:"

Num 21:18 — "The princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver, with their staves. And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah:"

Judg 9:21 — "And Jotham ran away, and fled, and went to Beer, and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother."

Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that where God gives His people water, there shall be singing.

expand to see more

Beer, the well, is a station of Israel and a town of refuge, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it as the proper name, distinct from the common noun for a well, that the reader may know the place where Israel sang over the water the LORD gave them in the desert.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the joyful provision of the LORD, who gathers His people and gives them water, and draws a song from their lips. With joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation (Isa 12:3). He who said, Gather the people together, and I will give them water, and brought forth the spring at the staves of the princes, is the same who is the fountain of living waters; and the song over the well of the wilderness is a foretaste of the new song of the redeemed, who drink of the river of His pleasures and praise Him for ever.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “a well,” Beer names the station where Israel sang over the water God gave them.

expand to see more

Beer — Hebrew be’ēr, “a well,” here a proper name.

It was a station of Israel beyond Arnon in the wilderness.

There the LORD gave the thirsting people water as He had promised.

Israel sang over it, Spring up, O well (Num 21:17).

A town of the same name sheltered Jotham from Abimelech (Judg 9:21).

Usage

"Like Israel at Beer, the people of God sing when He gives them water in the desert."

"With joy shall the redeemed draw water out of the wells of salvation."

"The LORD is pleased to use the obedience of His people in bringing forth the streams of His grace."
